**What you'll do**

1. Read what the CP-70 is and when it was made.
2. Learn how it makes its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.

5. Check yourself with a short quiz.

## What it is

- The **Yamaha CP-70** (1976, 73 keys) and **CP-80** (1978, 88 keys) are electric grand pianos, made until 1985 (Wikipedia, "Yamaha CP-70").
- They have a real piano action: "wooden keys to operate hammers that hit strings", but **no soundboard** (Wikipedia).
- It was built for touring: the harp lifts off the keys, and the legs pack into the lid (Wikipedia).

## Its sound

- "The strings are amplified by piezo-electric pickups mounted on the harp casting" (Wikipedia), like an acoustic guitar's pickups.
- The bass strings are much shorter than an acoustic piano's (Wikipedia). Short, thick strings are stiffer, so their overtones go sharp: a twangy bass (this page's model).
- Two or three strings for most notes, never exactly in tune with each other: a slow **beating** that makes it shimmer (this page's model).
- Its knobs here (Volume, a three-band EQ, Tremolo speed and depth) are from memory: **unverified**. Wikipedia names a graphic EQ on the later D models.

## The panel

The CP-70's panel drawn after the real one (not a copy; no logos). Turn the knobs, flip the switches, play the keys below it,
the computer keys or a MIDI keyboard. **Simple** shows every control as a slider, including the adjustments inside the instrument.
The sound is this site's own physical model (see [how it is modelled](epiano-compare.qmd#how-each-one-is-modelled)); nobody has
compared it with the real instrument. Facts come from the Wikipedia articles listed under Works Cited (read 2026-11-26). The service manuals were not read for these pages, so control legends and places that Wikipedia does not give are marked unverified.


## A guided tour

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;cp70&quot;}" data-riff="ballad">

**The plain CP-70.** Listen: a piano, but brighter and thinner, with no wooden body to it.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;cp70&quot;,&quot;detune&quot;:9}" data-riff="ballad">

**Strings wider apart.** Unison spread 9: the chorus-like shimmer it is known for.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;cp70&quot;,&quot;treble&quot;:8,&quot;mid&quot;:3,&quot;bass&quot;:6}" data-riff="ballad">

**EQ: Treble 8, Middle 3, Bass 6.** The 1980s ballad sparkle.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;cp70&quot;,&quot;trem&quot;:6,&quot;rate&quot;:5}" data-riff="ballad">

**Tremolo depth 6.** The level pulses (this control is unverified on the real panel).

</div>

## Famous tracks

Each video was checked on YouTube (oEmbed, 2026-11-26). Listen first, then press **▶** for a starting setting on the panel above.

### "That's All" (Genesis)

[▶ Genesis - That&#x27;s All (Official Music Video)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vzyn60Zns-E) on YouTube (Genesis).

Tony Banks's CP-70 (Wikipedia). A bouncing chord part, bright and percussive.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;cp70&quot;,&quot;treble&quot;:7,&quot;hard&quot;:6}" data-riff="soul">

**Starting setting** (CP-70): treble 7, hard 6. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

### "In Your Eyes" (Peter Gabriel)

[▶ Peter Gabriel - In Your Eyes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kU8OJAOMbPg) on YouTube (Peter Gabriel).

Wikipedia names it. Chords that ring and shimmer under the voice.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;cp70&quot;,&quot;detune&quot;:6,&quot;treble&quot;:6}" data-riff="ballad">

**Starting setting** (CP-70): detune 6, treble 6. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does it have instead of a soundboard?</b></p><ul><li>Piezo pickups</li><li>A magnetic pickup per key</li><li>A microphone</li><li>A speaker</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
```
